examples.japanese: {思慮|しりょ}{深|ぶか}い{人|ひと}だと{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think he is a thoughtful person.

examples.japanese: {思慮|しりょ}が{足|た}りない{行動|こうどう}だった。
examples.english: It was an action lacking in prudence.

examples.japanese: {重要|じゅうよう}な{決断|けつだん}は{十分|じゅうぶん}な{思慮|しりょ}を{重|かさ}ねてから{下|くだ}すべきだ。
examples.english: Important decisions should be made only after thorough deliberation.

notes:
Refers to deep, careful thought before making judgments or taking action. A formal word that appears frequently in compound expressions. Composed of {思|し} (think) and {慮|りょ} (consider, ponder).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {思慮|しりょ}{深|ぶか}い: thoughtful, prudent
- {思慮|しりょ}{分別|ふんべつ}: prudence and good judgment
- {思慮|しりょ}が{浅|あさ}い: lacking in thoughtfulness
- {思慮|しりょ}に{欠|か}ける: lacking prudence

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {配慮|はいりょ}: consideration, thoughtfulness — directed toward others' feelings or needs
- {熟慮|じゅくりょ}: careful deliberation — implies even deeper and more prolonged thought
- {考慮|こうりょ}: consideration — more neutral, taking something into account
